headline: Senior Jobs: Part-Time Work, Retirement Jobs & Paid Training in Rhode Island
intro: Find paid work across Rhode Island, with priority given to entry-level openings, employer-provided training and part-time schedules. Each record distinguishes required experience, physical duties, pay and verification status. General jobs are open to qualified applicants; this category serves older jobseekers and does not make jobs age-restricted.

programs.name: Senior Community Service Employment Program
programs.eligibility: Unemployed and family income generally at or below 125% of federal poverty level; program determines countable income and priority.
programs.benefit: Paid training at nonprofit/public host agencies, averaging 20 hours/week, at the highest applicable minimum wage; transition to unsubsidized work.
programs.contact: RI Governor's Workforce Board: 401-462-8860; dlt.gwbinfo@dlt.ri.gov. National program finder helpline: 877-872-5627.
programs.next_step: Use Resources for Workers 55+ on the RI GWB page or ask for the current SCSEP provider serving your town. Ask about openings, waiting list, host site, duties and income documents.
programs.notes: Not a permanent government job or guaranteed placement. The linked RI interest form could not be read by the research tool; no form was submitted.

incentives.name: Work Opportunity Tax Credit (WOTC)
incentives.description: IRS authorization page runs through December 31, 2025. RI accepts 2026-start applications as pending. Older age alone is not a target-group qualification.
incentives.notes: Do not promise a 2026 credit. Qualifying categories can include certain veterans, SSI recipients, vocational-rehabilitation referrals and long-term unemployed workers; exact conditions apply.

age_discrimination.summary: Age-discrimination protection generally begins at age 40. It applies to applicants as well as employees; retirement status does not remove protection.

federal.coverage: Private employers generally need 20+ employees; public/federal coverage and procedures differ.
federal.prohibited_conduct: Age-based hiring, firing, pay, promotion, assignments and training discrimination; retaliation for protected complaints is also prohibited.

rhode_island.coverage: Age 40+; employer definition generally includes businesses with four or more employees and state/political subdivisions, subject to statutory provisions.

filing.agency: Rhode Island Commission for Human Rights
filing.deadline: Generally one year from alleged harm to file a charge
EEOC Boston guidance gives 300 days for RI age-discrimination charges against covered employers; federal employees have a different process.

practical_steps: Preserve job advertisement and requisition number, application, emails, interview notes, dates, and relevant statements.
Write a dated factual timeline and record why you believe age affected the decision.
Contact RICHR or EEOC promptly; ask which claims and deadlines apply and whether both agencies are covered.
An inquiry, appointment request or ordinary email is not necessarily a filed charge. Confirm completion before the applicable deadline.
age_discrimination.editorial_note: General public information, not an assessment of a particular case. Do not label an employer discriminatory based on an unverified allegation.

disclaimer: Listings reflect public employer and official program information checked November 12, 2026. An online posting is not a guarantee of an unfilled position, interview, hiring speed, hours or benefits. Confirm details with the employer or program.
